sections.html:
The Allegheny Plateau carries Barbour County across north-central West Virginia, with Philippi as its seat. Rugged ground, drained by the Buckhannon, Middle Fork and Tygart Valley rivers, fills its 342.9 square miles. Highways U.S. 119 and U.S. 250 run north and south, and U.S. 33 touches the southern tip.

Residents numbered 15,461 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 15,414. In 2020 Philippi counted 2,928 people and Belington, the next-largest town, 1,804. A typical home is worth $106,600, 75.0% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median household earns $42,260.

Low ground along the Tygart Valley River holds most of Philippi, and floodwater has come into town repeatedly. November 1985 brought the most damaging flood. Since then the town has adopted a floodplain management plan.

Own a house on the river bottom? Before you list, do the following:

  • Check with your insurer or title company on whether the parcel lies in a mapped flood zone.
  • Pull together invoices for repairs after earlier water damage.
  • Prepare to disclose past water in the basement or crawl space to every buyer.
  • Find out if a buyer's lender will demand flood insurance.

Where flooding is possible, a financed sale drags, since both lender and insurer must approve. A cash buyer has no lender to satisfy, but a careful one will still weigh the risk.

sections.h2: How the state classifies and assesses property
sections.html:
Almost everything real and tangible in West Virginia is taxable. The July 1 snapshot of a parcel's owner, use and value governs the following calendar year. Values come from your county assessor, and the sheriff sends the ticket and takes the payment.

The constitution drops every parcel into one of four buckets:

  • Class I: intangibles and certain farm personal property.
  • Class II: the house its owner lives in and uses solely as a residence, along with farmland worked by the owner or a bona fide tenant.
  • Class III: everything else outside a municipality.
  • Class IV: everything else inside a municipality.

While you live there, the house is Class II. A buyer who rents it out or leaves it empty pushes it into Class III or IV, depending on whether it stands inside a municipality, and the bill can change. The taxing bodies are county boards of education, county commissions, municipalities and the State.

Calendar dateEvent for an owner
July 1Cutoff that locks in who owns the parcel, how it is used and what it is worth
July 15 or laterThe sheriff mails tax tickets
September 1Pay the first half by now to keep the discount
October 1An unpaid first half is delinquent and interest starts
December 1Homestead exemption applications close for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled
February 1 to February 28Assessment protests are heard by the county commission, acting as the board of equalization and review
March 1Pay the second half by now to keep the discount
April 1An unpaid second half is delinquent

To protest a value, appear before the county commission while it sits as the board of equalization and review. The board starts meeting February 1 and must finish by February 28, and the protest has to be filed ahead of the due date for that year's taxes. If the argument is over classification or taxability, you may take it to the Tax Commissioner under West Virginia Code 11-3-24a, which calls for a ruling by the end of February.

West Virginia Code 11-6B-3 shields $20,000 of a homestead's assessed value, the first slice, from ad valorem tax. Qualifying means being 65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled, and living in the house as a residence and nothing else.

You also need two straight calendar years of West Virginia residency before the tax year. A comparable exemption in another state rules you out.

The seller loses little here, but the buyer may feel it. Someone under 65 does not take over the exemption, and the bill may climb. Raise it with a financed buyer's agent early so the first ticket does not startle anyone.

Phone the sheriff's tax office for your balance first, then choose a closing date. Current-year tax still owed can be paid from the sale money, and the title company wants the amount in writing. The table above shows when each half goes delinquent and begins drawing interest, which tells you whether your bill has crossed the line.

Build a small folder before listing: your newest tax ticket, homestead exemption papers if you have them, and repair or water-damage records. Inherited house? Include papers that identify the heirs, because each may need to sign.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Barbour County
sections.html:
Expect the usual West Virginia closing sequence with no buyer's mortgage in it. You tell us about the house, we send a written offer, and you choose. After that an attorney or title company records the deed, clears liens and settles the tax due.

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses as-is, and the seller pays no fees, commissions or closing costs. Say no to an offer and you owe nothing.

Rural sellers keep hitting the same few snags:

  • Thin showing traffic on a listing, because buyers may have a long way to drive.
  • Aging houses with open questions about plumbing, roofing or septic.
  • Inherited property whose heirs live in several different states.

Cash removes showings and repair haggling, where listings often lose weeks. It cannot remove title work, so settle any tax balance and any lien ahead of the closing date.

Let the tax calendar guide your timing. Tickets show up in July and the first half is due in September, so a late-summer closing can land right beside a due date. A winter or spring closing sits close to the March 1 second installment. Whichever it is, learn from the sheriff's tax office what is paid, and settle with your buyer who covers which half.

For a fast sale, work in this order: confirm the tax balance, collect the deed and any lien papers, pick a date that suits you, and let the title company start its search. No lender is involved, so the date is mostly yours, limited only by how long title work takes.

When you call the tax office, have your parcel details and the name on the ticket in front of you. Ask three things: what is the balance, which half is it for, and has any interest been added. Write down the answers with the date of the call. If the house has been in a family for years, expect the file to carry older names, and allow a few extra days for the title company to sort that out. Philippi and Belington properties inside a municipality fall in Class IV when not owner-occupied, so confirm which class your parcel sits in before you quote a tax figure to a buyer.

faqs.q: What are the Barbour County tax due dates?
faqs.a: The sheriff issues tickets starting July 15. Half is due September 1 and half March 1, and a half left unpaid is delinquent from October 1 or April 1.

faqs.q: Where do I contest a Barbour County valuation?
faqs.a: Appear before the county commission when it convenes as the board of equalization and review, beginning February 1 and wrapping up by February 28. File before that year's taxes come due.

faqs.q: Who is eligible for the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Residents 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, living in the home. They exempt $20,000 of assessed value and must apply by December 1.

faqs.q: Can a house be sold while taxes are owed?
faqs.a: Yes, and the balance normally comes out of your proceeds at closing. Start by asking the sheriff's tax office what you owe.

faqs.q: What does a Cash Home Buyers purchase cost the seller?
faqs.a: Nothing. We buy houses as-is, you are not charged fees, commissions or closing costs, and turning down our offer is free.
